## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
At the beginning of the 1980s, he set up The Pavarotti International Voice Competition for young singers, performing with the winners in 1982 in excerpts of _La bohème_ and _L'elisir d'amore_. The second competition, in 1986, staged excerpts of _La bohème_ and _Un ballo in maschera_. To celebrate the 25th anniversary of his career, he brought the winners of the competition to Italy for gala performances of _La bohème_ in Modena and [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa"), and then to China, where they staged performances of _La bohème_ in Beijing ([Peking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peking "Peking")). To conclude the visit, Pavarotti performed the inaugural concert in the [Great Hall of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Hall_of_the_People "Great Hall of the People") before 10,000 people, receiving a [standing ovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_ovation "Standing ovation") for nine high Cs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-37) The third competition in 1989 again staged performances of _L'elisir d'amore_ and _Un ballo in maschera_. The winners of the fifth competition accompanied Pavarotti in performances in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") in 1997.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
texts.20:
## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In the mid-1980s, Pavarotti returned to two opera houses that had provided him with important breakthroughs, the [Vienna State Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_State_Opera "Vienna State Opera") and [La Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Scala "La Scala"). Vienna saw Pavarotti as Rodolfo in _La bohème_ with [Carlos Kleiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Kleiber "Carlos Kleiber") conducting, and again Mirella Freni was Mimi; as Nemorino in _L'elisir d'amore_; as Radames in _Aida_ conducted by Lorin Maazel; as Rodolfo in _Luisa Miller_; and as Gustavo in _Un ballo in maschera_ conducted by Claudio Abbado. In 1996, Pavarotti appeared for the last time at the Staatsoper in _Andrea Chénier_. Throughout the 1980s and 90s, promoters [Tibor Rudas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibor_Rudas "Tibor Rudas") and [Harvey Goldsmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Goldsmith "Harvey Goldsmith") booked Pavarotti into increasingly larger venues.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Vincenzo_Mollica%2C_Pavarotti%2C_Lucio_Dalla_e_Zucchero_al_Pavarotti_e_friends_1992.jpg/250px-Vincenzo_Mollica%2C_Pavarotti%2C_Lucio_Dalla_e_Zucchero_al_Pavarotti_e_friends_1992.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vincenzo_Mollica,_Pavarotti,_Lucio_Dalla_e_Zucchero_al_Pavarotti_e_friends_1992.jpg)

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
From left: journalist Vincenzo Mollica, Pavarotti, [Lucio Dalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucio_Dalla "Lucio Dalla") and [Zucchero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zucchero_Fornaciari "Zucchero Fornaciari") on the first edition of _[Pavarotti & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavarotti\_&\_Friends "Pavarotti & Friends")_ (1992)
In 1985, Pavarotti sang Radames at La Scala opposite Maria Chiara in a Luca Ronconi production conducted by Maazel, recorded on video. His performance of the aria "Celeste Aida" received a two-minute ovation on the opening night.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He was reunited with Mirella Freni for the San Francisco Opera production of _La bohème_ in 1988, also recorded on video. In 1992, La Scala saw Pavarotti in a new Zeffirelli production of _Don Carlos_, conducted by Riccardo Muti.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-38)
texts.22:
## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
Pavarotti became even better known throughout the world in 1990 when his rendition of the aria "[Nessun dorma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nessun_dorma "Nessun dorma")" from [Giacomo Puccini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Puccini "Giacomo Puccini")'s _[Turandot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turandot "Turandot")_ was taken as the theme song of [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s coverage of the [1990 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup") in Italy. The aria achieved pop status, became the World Cup soundtrack, and remained his trademark song.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-39) This was followed by the first [Three Tenors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Tenors "Three Tenors") concert, held on the eve of the [1990 FIFA World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "1990 FIFA World Cup Final") at the ancient [Baths of Caracalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baths_of_Caracalla "Baths of Caracalla") in Rome with fellow tenors [Plácido Domingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pl%C3%A1cido_Domingo "Plácido Domingo") and [José Carreras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Carreras "José Carreras") and conductor [Zubin Mehta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zubin_Mehta "Zubin Mehta").
texts.23:
## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
The performance for the World Cup closing concert captivated a global audience, and it became the biggest-selling classical record of all time.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-40) A highlight of the concert, in which Pavarotti sang the opening verses using extended vocal runs for di Capua's "['O sole mio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'O_sole_mio "'O sole mio")" and which was in turn perfectly repeated note-for-note by Domingo and Carreras. The recorded album sold millions of copies,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-41) and the [first Three Tenors recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carreras_Domingo_Pavarotti_in_Concert "Carreras Domingo Pavarotti in Concert") became the best-selling classical album of all time.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-42) Throughout the 1990s, Pavarotti appeared in outdoor concerts, [including his televised concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavarotti_in_the_Park "Pavarotti in the Park") in London's [Hyde Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London "Hyde Park, London"), which drew a record attendance of 150,000.
texts.24:
## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In June 1993, more than 500,000 listeners gathered for his free performance on the Great Lawn of New York's [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), while millions more around the world watched on television.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-43) The following September, in the shadow of the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower") in Paris, he sang for an estimated crowd of 300,000.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-44) Following on from the original 1990 concert, the Three Tenors concerts were held during the three subsequent [FIFA World Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_finals "List of FIFA World Cup finals"), in 1994 in Los Angeles, 1998 in Paris, and 2002 in Yokohama.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-FIFA-45)
[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg/250px-Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg)
[Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John") and Pavarotti in Modena, 1996

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In September 1995, Pavarotti performed Schubert's [Ave Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ave_Maria_(Schubert) "Ave Maria (Schubert)") along with [Dolores O'Riordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_O'Riordan "Dolores O'Riordan"); [Diana, Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Diana, Princess of Wales"), who attended the live performance, told O'Riordan that the song brought her to tears.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-46)
In 1995, Pavarotti's friends, [Lara Saint Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lara_Saint_Paul "Lara Saint Paul") (as Lara Cariaggi) and her husband showman Pier Quinto Cariaggi, who had produced and organised Pavarotti's 1990 FIFA World Cup Celebration Concert at the [PalaTrussardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PalaSharp "PalaSharp") in Milan, produced and wrote the television documentary _The Best is Yet to Come_, an extensive biography about the life of Pavarotti. Lara Saint Paul was the interviewer for the documentary with Pavarotti, who spoke candidly about his life and career.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-47)
texts.26:
## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
Pavarotti earned a reputation as "The King of Cancellations" by frequently backing out of performances, and his unreliable nature led to poor relationships with some opera houses.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-48) This was brought into focus in 1989 when [Ardis Krainik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardis_Krainik "Ardis Krainik") of the [Lyric Opera of Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyric_Opera_of_Chicago "Lyric Opera of Chicago") severed the house's 15-year relationship with the tenor.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-Ref-1-49) Over an eight-year period, Pavarotti had cancelled 26 out of 41 scheduled appearances at the Lyric, and the decisive move by Krainik to ban him for life was well noted throughout the opera world,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-50) after the performer walked away from a season premiere less than two weeks before rehearsals began, saying pain from a sciatic nerve required two months of treatment.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-51) On 12 December 1998, he became the first (and, to date, only) opera singer to perform on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, singing alongside [Vanessa L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_L._Williams "Vanessa L. Williams").
texts.27:

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
Pavarotti began his career as a tenor in smaller regional Italian opera houses. After winning the Achille Peri International Competition, he made his debut as Rodolfo in _[La bohème](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_boh%C3%A8me "La bohème")_ at the [Teatro Municipale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_Municipale_di_Reggio "Teatro Municipale di Reggio") in [Reggio Emilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggio_Emilia "Reggio Emilia") in April 1961, conducted by [Francesco Molinari-Pradelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Molinari-Pradelli "Francesco Molinari-Pradelli") and staged by [Mafalda Favero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mafalda_Favero "Mafalda Favero").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-tenor-4) His first known recording of "[Che gelida manina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Che_gelida_manina "Che gelida manina")" was recorded during this performance.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-21)

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
In December 1961, Pavarotti made his first international appearance in _[La traviata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_traviata "La traviata")_ in [Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-23) On 23 February 1963, he debuted at the [Vienna State Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_State_Opera "Vienna State Opera") in the same role. In March and April 1963, Pavarotti performed again in Vienna as Rodolfo and as Duca di Mantova in _[Rigoletto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigoletto "Rigoletto")_.

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
The same year, he performed his first solo non-opera concert outside Italy when he sang in [Dundalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundalk "Dundalk"), Ireland, for the St Cecilia's Gramophone Society.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-dundalk-24) He was engaged by the Dublin Grand Opera Society to sing The Duke of Mantua in Verdi's [Rigoletto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigoletto "Rigoletto") in May and June,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-dundalk-24) and his [Royal Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Royal_Opera "The Royal Opera") debut, where he replaced an indisposed [Giuseppe Di Stefano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Di_Stefano "Giuseppe Di Stefano") as Rodolfo.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-aboutvoice-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-26) In September 1963, he made his debut at Covent Garden in La Boheme, which gave his career a boost.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-27)

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
In 1964, Pavarotti appeared as Idamante in _[Idomeneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idomeneo "Idomeneo")_ at [Glyndebourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyndebourne_Festival_Opera "Glyndebourne Festival Opera")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-28) and was engaged by the Dublin Grand Opera Society to sing Rodolfo in [Giacomo Puccini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Puccini "Giacomo Puccini")'s _[La bohème](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_boh%C3%A8me "La bohème")_ and Alfredo in Giuseppe Verdi's _[La Traviata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Traviata "La Traviata")_. Reviewers favourably comment on his singing.

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
Pavarotti sang with Joan Sutherland when he made his American début with the [Greater Miami Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Grand_Opera "Florida Grand Opera") in February 1965, singing in [Gaetano Donizetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaetano_Donizetti "Gaetano Donizetti")'s _[Lucia di Lammermoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucia\_di\_Lammermoor "Lucia di Lammermoor")_ on the stage of the [Miami-Dade County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami-Dade_County "Miami-Dade County") Auditorium in Miami. The tenor that was scheduled to perform that night became ill with no understudy. Sutherland recommended Pavarotti as he was acquainted with the role. On 28 April, Pavarotti made his [La Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Scala "La Scala") debut in the revival of the [Franco Zeffirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Zeffirelli "Franco Zeffirelli") production of _La bohème_, with his childhood friend [Mirella Freni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirella_Freni "Mirella Freni") singing Mimi and [Herbert von Karajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_von_Karajan "Herbert von Karajan") conducting. Karajan had requested the singer's engagement.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-tenor-4)

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
[Joan Sutherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Sutherland "Joan Sutherland") and her conductor husband, [Richard Bonynge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Bonynge "Richard Bonynge") sought a tall tenor to take along on their 1965 tour to Australia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-tenor-4)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-aboutvoice-25) During the Australia tour in summer 1965, Sutherland and Pavarotti sang forty performances over two months. Pavarotti later credited Sutherland for the breathing and diaphragm technique that sustained him through his career.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-tenor-4)
After the extended Australian tour, he returned to La Scala, where he added Tebaldo from _[I Capuleti e i Montecchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Capuleti\_e\_i\_Montecchi "I Capuleti e i Montecchi")_ to his repertoire on 26 March 1966, with [Giacomo Aragall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Aragall "Giacomo Aragall") as Romeo.
His first appearance as Tonio in Donizetti's _[La fille du régiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_fille\_du\_r%C3%A9giment "La fille du régiment")_ took place at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, on 2 June 1966. In this performance, he was the first tenor to deliver nine natural high Cs in the aria "Ah! mes amis".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-tenor-4)

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
He scored another major triumph in Rome on 20 November 1969 when he sang in _[I Lombardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Lombardi\_alla\_prima\_crociata "I Lombardi alla prima crociata")_ opposite [Renata Scotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renata_Scotto "Renata Scotto"). This was recorded on a private label and widely distributed, as were various recordings of his _I Capuleti e i Montecchi_, usually with Aragall. Early commercial recordings included a recital of Donizetti (the aria from _[Don Sebastiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dom\_S%C3%A9bastien "Dom Sébastien")_ were particularly highly regarded) and [Verdi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Verdi "Giuseppe Verdi")[arias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aria "Aria"), as well as a complete _[L'elisir d'amore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'elisir\_d'amore "L'elisir d'amore")_ with Sutherland.
His breakthrough in the United States came on 17 February 1972, in a production of _La fille du régiment_ at New York's [Metropolitan Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera "Metropolitan Opera"), in which he hit nine [high Cs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenor_C "Tenor C") in the signature [aria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aria "Aria") and had seventeen curtain calls.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-29) This earned him the nickname "King of the High Cs".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-30)

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
Pavarotti sang his international [recital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert#Recital "Concert") début at [William Jewell College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jewell_College "William Jewell College") in [Liberty, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty,_Missouri "Liberty, Missouri"), on 1 February 1973, as part of the college's Fine Arts Program, now known as the Harriman–Jewell Series.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-:0-31) According to his manager at the time, Pavarotti clutched a handkerchief throughout this recital because he had a lingering cold.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-32) Pavarotti himself explained that he needed the handkerchief, since he didn't know what to do with his hands.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-:0-31) The prop became a signature part of his solo performances.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-33) He began to give frequent television performances, starting with his performances as Rodolfo (_La bohème_) in the first [Live from the Met](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_from_the_Met "Live from the Met") telecast in March 1977, which attracted one of the largest audiences ever for a televised opera.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-34) He won [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") awards and [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_disc "Platinum disc") and [gold discs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_disc "Gold disc") for his performances.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Biography
### Career: 1960s–1970s
In 1976, Pavarotti debuted at the [Salzburg Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salzburg_Festival "Salzburg Festival"), appearing in a solo recital on 31 July, accompanied by pianist Leone Magiera. Pavarotti returned to the festival in 1978 with a recital and as the Italian singer in _[Der Rosenkavalier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der\_Rosenkavalier "Der Rosenkavalier")_ in 1983 with _[Idomeneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idomeneo "Idomeneo")_, and both in 1985 and 1988 with solo recitals. In 1979, he was profiled in a cover story in the weekly magazine _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-35) That same year saw Pavarotti's return to the [Vienna State Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_State_Opera "Vienna State Opera") after an absence of fourteen years. With Herbert von Karajan conducting, Pavarotti sang Manrico in _[Il trovatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_trovatore "Il trovatore")_. In 1978, he appeared in a solo recital on _[Live from Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_from\_Lincoln\_Center "Live from Lincoln Center")_.

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
At the beginning of the 1980s, he set up The Pavarotti International Voice Competition for young singers, performing with the winners in 1982 in excerpts of _La bohème_ and _L'elisir d'amore_. The second competition, in 1986, staged excerpts of _La bohème_ and _Un ballo in maschera_. To celebrate the 25th anniversary of his career, he brought the winners of the competition to Italy for gala performances of _La bohème_ in Modena and [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa"), and then to China, where they staged performances of _La bohème_ in Beijing ([Peking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peking "Peking")). To conclude the visit, Pavarotti performed the inaugural concert in the [Great Hall of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Hall_of_the_People "Great Hall of the People") before 10,000 people, receiving a [standing ovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_ovation "Standing ovation") for nine high Cs.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-37) The third competition in 1989 again staged performances of _L'elisir d'amore_ and _Un ballo in maschera_. The winners of the fifth competition accompanied Pavarotti in performances in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") in 1997.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In the mid-1980s, Pavarotti returned to two opera houses that had provided him with important breakthroughs, the [Vienna State Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_State_Opera "Vienna State Opera") and [La Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Scala "La Scala"). Vienna saw Pavarotti as Rodolfo in _La bohème_ with [Carlos Kleiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Kleiber "Carlos Kleiber") conducting, and again Mirella Freni was Mimi; as Nemorino in _L'elisir d'amore_; as Radames in _Aida_ conducted by Lorin Maazel; as Rodolfo in _Luisa Miller_; and as Gustavo in _Un ballo in maschera_ conducted by Claudio Abbado. In 1996, Pavarotti appeared for the last time at the Staatsoper in _Andrea Chénier_. Throughout the 1980s and 90s, promoters [Tibor Rudas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibor_Rudas "Tibor Rudas") and [Harvey Goldsmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Goldsmith "Harvey Goldsmith") booked Pavarotti into increasingly larger venues.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
Pavarotti became even better known throughout the world in 1990 when his rendition of the aria "[Nessun dorma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nessun_dorma "Nessun dorma")" from [Giacomo Puccini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giacomo_Puccini "Giacomo Puccini")'s _[Turandot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turandot "Turandot")_ was taken as the theme song of [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s coverage of the [1990 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup") in Italy. The aria achieved pop status, became the World Cup soundtrack, and remained his trademark song.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-39) This was followed by the first [Three Tenors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Tenors "Three Tenors") concert, held on the eve of the [1990 FIFA World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "1990 FIFA World Cup Final") at the ancient [Baths of Caracalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baths_of_Caracalla "Baths of Caracalla") in Rome with fellow tenors [Plácido Domingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pl%C3%A1cido_Domingo "Plácido Domingo") and [José Carreras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Carreras "José Carreras") and conductor [Zubin Mehta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zubin_Mehta "Zubin Mehta").

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
The performance for the World Cup closing concert captivated a global audience, and it became the biggest-selling classical record of all time.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-40) A highlight of the concert, in which Pavarotti sang the opening verses using extended vocal runs for di Capua's "['O sole mio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'O_sole_mio "'O sole mio")" and which was in turn perfectly repeated note-for-note by Domingo and Carreras. The recorded album sold millions of copies,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-41) and the [first Three Tenors recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carreras_Domingo_Pavarotti_in_Concert "Carreras Domingo Pavarotti in Concert") became the best-selling classical album of all time.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-42) Throughout the 1990s, Pavarotti appeared in outdoor concerts, [including his televised concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavarotti_in_the_Park "Pavarotti in the Park") in London's [Hyde Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London "Hyde Park, London"), which drew a record attendance of 150,000.

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In June 1993, more than 500,000 listeners gathered for his free performance on the Great Lawn of New York's [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), while millions more around the world watched on television.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-43) The following September, in the shadow of the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower") in Paris, he sang for an estimated crowd of 300,000.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-44) Following on from the original 1990 concert, the Three Tenors concerts were held during the three subsequent [FIFA World Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_finals "List of FIFA World Cup finals"), in 1994 in Los Angeles, 1998 in Paris, and 2002 in Yokohama.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-FIFA-45)

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
In September 1995, Pavarotti performed Schubert's [Ave Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ave_Maria_(Schubert) "Ave Maria (Schubert)") along with [Dolores O'Riordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_O'Riordan "Dolores O'Riordan"); [Diana, Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Diana, Princess of Wales"), who attended the live performance, told O'Riordan that the song brought her to tears.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-46)
In 1995, Pavarotti's friends, [Lara Saint Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lara_Saint_Paul "Lara Saint Paul") (as Lara Cariaggi) and her husband showman Pier Quinto Cariaggi, who had produced and organised Pavarotti's 1990 FIFA World Cup Celebration Concert at the [PalaTrussardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PalaSharp "PalaSharp") in Milan, produced and wrote the television documentary _The Best is Yet to Come_, an extensive biography about the life of Pavarotti. Lara Saint Paul was the interviewer for the documentary with Pavarotti, who spoke candidly about his life and career.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-47)

## Biography
### Career: 1980s–1990s
Pavarotti earned a reputation as "The King of Cancellations" by frequently backing out of performances, and his unreliable nature led to poor relationships with some opera houses.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-48) This was brought into focus in 1989 when [Ardis Krainik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardis_Krainik "Ardis Krainik") of the [Lyric Opera of Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyric_Opera_of_Chicago "Lyric Opera of Chicago") severed the house's 15-year relationship with the tenor.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-Ref-1-49) Over an eight-year period, Pavarotti had cancelled 26 out of 41 scheduled appearances at the Lyric, and the decisive move by Krainik to ban him for life was well noted throughout the opera world,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-50) after the performer walked away from a season premiere less than two weeks before rehearsals began, saying pain from a sciatic nerve required two months of treatment.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-51) On 12 December 1998, he became the first (and, to date, only) opera singer to perform on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, singing alongside [Vanessa L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_L._Williams "Vanessa L. Williams").

## Other work
### Humanitarianism
#### Humanitarian honours
Also in 2001, Pavarotti was chosen one of that year's five recipients by the President and First Lady as an honoree for their lifetime achievements in the arts at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), followed by the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"); the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors"), He was surprised by the appearance of [Secretary-General of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations") and that year's winner of the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), who lauded him for his contribution to humankind. Six months prior, Pavarotti had held a large charity concert for Afghan refugees, particularly children in his home town of Modena, Italy.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-Kennedy_Center_Honors1-87)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-88)
Other honours he received include the _"Freedom of London Award"_ and The [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross")_"Award for Services to Humanity"_, for his work in raising money for that organisation, and the 1998 _"[MusiCares Person of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusiCares\_Person\_of\_the\_Year "MusiCares Person of the Year")"_, given to humanitarian heroes by the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti#cite_note-89)

The emotional depth is impossible to fully articulate, but you feel it immediately on stage. Every role, not just the ones about motherhood, suddenly has this weight, this perspective about what truly matters. We just performed Madama Butterfly with @louislohraseb . That final scene where Cio-Cio San says goodbye to her child feels completely different now. The emotion isn't something I have to search for or manufacture. It's just there. You don't have to be a parent to access profound emotional depth as a performer. This is simply what changed for me personally. Motherhood gave me this bottomless well to draw from, this clarity on what's important. It has reshaped how I approach every single role I sing.

# Italian Opera Singer Divorced Twice Five Children
Only when I decided to fully be at PEACE with my path, did I find peace WITHIN MYSELF and started ENJOYING everything much better. No one defines my WORTH. I am an opera singer whether anyone approves it or not, and I will keep creating my art and refining my craft for as long as I am here. I could choose to work in something more “stable”... But my HEART is full when I SING. REJECTIONS are not failures - the moment I understood that… MY LIFE CHANGED. I accept them as part of the journey, learning and growing from them. “What if?” I don’t want this question to hunt me for the rest of my life. This path takes TIME - sometimes huge success seems like it happened overnight, but it actually happened over time - practicing, refining, discovering, diving deep. The opera journey is actually my soul’s GROWTH journey - I want to dive deep and figure it out, and not run away from the desire of my SOUL. There are small SIGNS on my way which show me that everything is synchronized, and ALIGNED with who I am. I truly LOVE singing, I love being on stage. MUSIC, to me, is sacred - a spiritual space beyond words. During the past 6 years I had so many reasons to quit… Covid, cancellations, motherhood, wars… but I stayed against all odds. Keep going for your dreams✨ I am building a community of singers where we share ideas about mindset, networking, and the singing path.
If this resonates with you - comment DREAM,

**Valerie June Carter Cash** (June 23, 1929– May 15, 2003) was an American country singer, songwriter, comedian, actress, and author. A five-time [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") winner, she was a member of the [Carter Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Family "Carter Family") and the second wife of singer [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash"). Before her marriage, she performed as **June Carter**, a name she continued to use professionally, including on songwriting credits. She played guitar, [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo"), harmonica, and [autoharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoharp "Autoharp"), and acted in several films and television shows. In 2009, she was posthumously inducted into the Christian Music Hall of Fame, and in 2025, she was named a posthumous inductee into the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Valerie June Carter was born on June 23, 1929, in [Maces Spring, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maces_Spring,_Virginia "Maces Spring, Virginia"), to [Maybelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybelle_Carter "Maybelle Carter") (née Addington) and [Ezra Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Carter "Ezra Carter").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-1) Her mother performed country music with her sister-in-law [Sara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Carter "Sara Carter") and brother [A. P. Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._P._Carter "A. P. Carter"). Carter began performing with the Carter Family at age 10, in 1939.
In March 1943, when the Carter Family trio stopped recording at the end of the [WBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBT_(AM) "WBT (AM)") contract, Maybelle, encouraged by her husband Ezra, formed "The Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle." Helen played accordion, Anita played bass fiddle, and Carter played autoharp and served as front person and comedian. The group first aired on [WRNL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRNL "WRNL") in [Richmond, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia"), on June 1. Doc Addington and Carl McConnell, Maybelle's brother and cousin, known as "The Virginia Boys", joined them in late 1945.

At 16, Carter was a co-announcer with Ken Allyn and read commercials for Red Star Flour, Martha White, and [Thalhimers Department Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalhimers "Thalhimers").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-JUNE_CARTER_CASH_BIOGRAPHY-2) In 1946, the Carters and Doc and Carl performed show dates within driving distance of Richmond, across [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware"), and [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). Carter attended [John Marshall High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marshall_High_School_(Richmond,_Virginia) "John Marshall High School (Richmond, Virginia)") during this period.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-3) She later said she had to work harder at her music than her sisters, but she had her own special talent: comedy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-4) A highlight of the road shows was her "Aunt Polly" routine. With her thin, lanky frame, she often played a comedic foil alongside Opry stars [Faron Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faron_Young "Faron Young") and [Webb Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Pierce "Webb Pierce"). Carl McConnell wrote that Carter was "a natural-born clown, if there ever was one". She revived Aunt Polly for the 1976 TV _Johnny Cash & Friends_.

After Doc and Carl left the music business in late 1946, Maybelle and her daughters moved to [Sunshine Sue Workman's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine_Sue "Sunshine Sue") "Old Dominion Barn Dance" on [WRVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRVA_(AM) "WRVA (AM)") in Richmond. They later moved to [WNOX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNOX "WNOX") in [Knoxville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville,_Tennessee "Knoxville, Tennessee"), where they met [Chet Atkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chet_Atkins "Chet Atkins") while working with [Homer and Jethro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_and_Jethro "Homer and Jethro").
In 1949, the Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle, with Atkins as lead guitarist, lived in [Springfield, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Missouri "Springfield, Missouri"), and performed regularly at [KWTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KWTO_(AM) "KWTO (AM)"). Ezra declined repeated offers from the [Grand Ole Opry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Ole_Opry "Grand Ole Opry") to move the act to [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee") because the Opry would not allow Atkins to accompany them onstage. Studio musicians feared Atkins would displace them as a first‑call player. In 1950, Opry management relented, and the group, with Atkins, joined the Opry. The family befriended [Hank Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Williams "Hank Williams") and [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), and Carter met [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").
During the 1960s and 1970s, Carter and her sisters, with Maybelle and Sara joining at times, reclaimed the name "The Carter Family" for their act.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg/250px-JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg)
Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash in 1969
Carter was married three times and had one child with each husband. All three of her children went on to have successful careers in country music. She married her first husband, [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer [Carl Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Smith_(country_musician) "Carl Smith (country musician)"), on July 9, 1952; they divorced in 1956. Together they wrote "Time's A-Wastin". They had a daughter, Rebecca Carlene Smith, known professionally as [Carlene Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlene_Carter "Carlene Carter"), a country musician.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Johnny_Cash_and_June_Carter_Cash_Marriage_Profile-5)
Carter married her second husband, Edwin "Rip" Nix, a police officer and former football player, on November 11, 1957. Their daughter, [Rosie Nix Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Nix_Adams "Rosie Nix Adams"), was born on July 13, 1958, and became a country and rock singer. The couple divorced in 1966 because of Carter's affair with [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").

Carter and the entire Carter Family had performed with Johnny Cash for a number of years. In 1968, Cash proposed to Carter during a live performance at the [London Ice House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Ice_House "London Ice House"), then known as "Treasure Island Gardens", or simply "The Gardens", in [London, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London,_Ontario "London, Ontario"). They married on March 1 in [Franklin, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Kentucky "Franklin, Kentucky").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) They had one son, [John Carter Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carter_Cash "John Carter Cash"), who became a musician, songwriter, and producer. The couple remained married until her death in May 2003, four months before Cash died.
She also gained four stepdaughters from Cash's previous marriage to Vivian Liberto, including [Cindy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Cash "Cindy Cash") and [Rosanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash").
Carter's distant cousin, 39th U.S. president [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter"), became closely acquainted with Cash and Carter and maintained their friendship throughout their lifetimes. In a June 1977 speech, Jimmy acknowledged that Carter was his distant cousin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarter19781115_(Conference_on_HIRE,_June_14)-7)

Carter also had close relationships with a number of entertainers, including [Audrey Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audrey_Williams "Audrey Williams"), [James Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Dean "James Dean"), [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8)[Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-9)[Jessi Colter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessi_Colter "Jessi Colter"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), Elvis Presley,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8) Robert Duvall, and [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-10)
At the end of her life, she and her husband attended the First [Baptist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist_Church "Baptist Church") in [Hendersonville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville,_Tennessee "Hendersonville, Tennessee").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-11)

In April 2003, Carter Cash was diagnosed with a [leaky heart valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valvular_heart_disease "Valvular heart disease"), and doctors told her that valve replacement surgery was the only solution.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-12) She had the surgery on May 7; however, complications arose, and her health deteriorated rapidly over the next few days. She died on May 15, 2003 at age 73.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) Public funeral services were held at the First Baptist Church in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-14) At Carter Cash's funeral, her stepdaughter [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash") stated, "If being a wife were a corporation, June would have been a [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO"). It was her most treasured role."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-15)
Johnny Cash died of complications from diabetes on September 12. Carter Cash's daughter, Rosie Nix Adams, died from accidental [carbon monoxide poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide_poisoning "Carbon monoxide poisoning") in a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") that had been [converted into a campervan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_van "Conversion van"), on October 24, at age 45.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-16) All three are buried at [Hendersonville Memory Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville_Memory_Gardens "Hendersonville Memory Gardens") near their home in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-17)

**Domenico Modugno** (born January 9, 1928 – died August 6, 1994) was a famous Italian singer, songwriter, and actor. Later in his life, he also became a member of the [Italian Parliament](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italian_Parliament "Italian Parliament"). He is best known for his huge international hit song from 1958, "Nel blu dipinto di blu" (often called "Volare"). This song won him two [Grammy Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"). Many people see him as the first true Italian _cantautore_, which means a singer-songwriter who writes and performs their own songs.

## Domenico Modugno's Early Life
Domenico Modugno was born in [Polignano a Mare](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare "Polignano a Mare"), Italy, on January 9, 1928. He was the youngest of four children. His father, Vito Cosimo Modugno, worked as a police commander, and his mother, Pasqua Lorusso, was a housewife.
When Domenico was nine, his family moved to San Pietro Vernotico. There, he went to primary school and learned the local dialect. He later attended secondary school in Lecce.

## Domenico Modugno's Music Career
While still a student, Domenico Modugno started acting in films. His first taste of fame came in 1957 when his song "Lazzarella" placed second in a big Italian music contest called the Festival della Canzone Napoletana.
The biggest moment of his career happened in 1958. He entered the Sanremo Music Festival with a song he co-wrote called "Nel blu dipinto di blu". This song won the contest and became a massive hit all over the world. It sold over 22 million copies and won two [Grammy Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"). The song also represented Italy in the 1958 Eurovision Song Contest, where it finished third.
[![Image 3: Eurovision Song Contest 1958 - Domenico Modugno](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7f/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png/300px-Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)
Domenico Modugno singing "Nel blu, dipinto di blu" at the Eurovision Song Contest 1958.
Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival again in 1959 with "Piove" (also known as "Ciao, ciao bambina"). He also came in second place in 1960 with "Libero." He represented Italy in the Eurovision Song Contest again in 1959. Later, his song "Io" was covered by [Elvis Presley](https://kids.kiddle.co/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") in English, titled "Ask Me."
In 1962, Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival for a third time with "Addio... addio...." He returned to Eurovision in 1966 with "Dio, come ti amo." Other artists like [Sergio Franchi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sergio_Franchi "Sergio Franchi") and Jack Jones later recorded this song.

## Domenico Modugno's Music Career
Besides singing, Modugno acted in many movies, appearing in 44 films. He also produced two films, including _Tutto è musica_ (1963), which was about his own life. In the 1970s, he started focusing more on classical music and acting in modern operas.

## Domenico Modugno's Later Years
In 1984, Domenico Modugno had a serious health issue that affected his ability to perform. This led him to focus on his recovery.
From 1986, he became very active in fighting for the rights of people with disabilities. In June 1987, he was elected to the Italian Parliament as a representative for [Turin](https://kids.kiddle.co/Turin "Turin"). He was part of the Radical Party, a group focused on social issues. He spoke out against unfair treatment of patients in hospitals and supported campaigns for human rights.
Modugno returned to music in 1992–1993. His last song was "Delfini" (meaning "Dolphins"), which he sang with his son, Massimo, in 1993.
Domenico Modugno passed away on August 6, 1994, at the age of 66. He died from a heart attack at his home on the island of [Lampedusa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lampedusa "Lampedusa"), south of Sicily. His beautiful beach house was later put up for sale.

Here are some of Domenico Modugno's well-known songs:

*   "Lazzarella"  
*   "Nel blu dipinto di blu" – also known as "Volare" (Sanremo winner, 1958)  
*   "Buon Natale A Tutto Il Mondo" (1958, with [Ennio Morricone](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone"))  
*   "La lontananza"

*   "Sopra i tetti azzurri del mio pazzo amore"

Domenico Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival four times. Here are his winning years and other notable entries:

*   1968 "Il posto mio"  
*   1971 "Come stai?"  
*   1972 "Un calcio alla città"  
*   1974 "Questa è la mia vita" (second place)

## Domenico Modugno's Songs
### Sanremo Music Festival Wins
Domenico Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival four times. Here are his winning years and other notable entries:
*   1958 "Nel blu dipinto di blu" (winner)  
*   1959 "Piove (Ciao, ciao bambina)" (winner)  
*   1960 "Libero" (second place)  
*   1962 "Addio... addio..." (winner)  
*   1964 "Che me ne importa a me" (second place)  
*   1966 "Dio, come ti amo" (winner)  
*   1967 "Sopra i tetti azzurri del mio pazzo amore"  
*   1968 "Il posto mio"  
*   1971 "Come stai?"  
*   1972 "Un calcio alla città"  
*   1974 "Questa è la mia vita" (second place)

**Valerie June Carter Cash** (June 23, 1929– May 15, 2003) was an American country singer, songwriter, comedian, actress, and author. A five-time [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") winner, she was a member of the [Carter Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Family "Carter Family") and the second wife of singer [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash"). Before her marriage, she performed as **June Carter**, a name she continued to use professionally, including on songwriting credits. She played guitar, [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo"), harmonica, and [autoharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoharp "Autoharp"), and acted in several films and television shows. In 2009, she was posthumously inducted into the Christian Music Hall of Fame, and in 2025, she was named a posthumous inductee into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
texts.2:
Valerie June Carter was born on June 23, 1929, in [Maces Spring, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maces_Spring,_Virginia "Maces Spring, Virginia"), to [Maybelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybelle_Carter "Maybelle Carter") (née Addington) and [Ezra Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Carter "Ezra Carter").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-1) Her mother performed country music with her sister-in-law [Sara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Carter "Sara Carter") and brother [A. P. Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._P._Carter "A. P. Carter"). Carter began performing with the Carter Family at age 10, in 1939.
In March 1943, when the Carter Family trio stopped recording at the end of the [WBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBT_(AM) "WBT (AM)") contract, Maybelle, encouraged by her husband Ezra, formed "The Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle." Helen played accordion, Anita played bass fiddle, and Carter played autoharp and served as front person and comedian. The group first aired on [WRNL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRNL "WRNL") in [Richmond, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia"), on June 1. Doc Addington and Carl McConnell, Maybelle's brother and cousin, known as "The Virginia Boys", joined them in late 1945.
texts.3: At 16, Carter was a co-announcer with Ken Allyn and read commercials for Red Star Flour, Martha White, and [Thalhimers Department Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalhimers "Thalhimers").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-JUNE_CARTER_CASH_BIOGRAPHY-2) In 1946, the Carters and Doc and Carl performed show dates within driving distance of Richmond, across [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware"), and [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). Carter attended [John Marshall High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marshall_High_School_(Richmond,_Virginia) "John Marshall High School (Richmond, Virginia)") during this period.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-3) She later said she had to work harder at her music than her sisters, but she had her own special talent: comedy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-4) A highlight of the road shows was her "Aunt Polly" routine. With her thin, lanky frame, she often played a comedic foil alongside Opry stars [Faron Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faron_Young "Faron Young") and [Webb Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Pierce "Webb Pierce"). Carl McConnell wrote that Carter was "a natural-born clown, if there ever was one". She revived Aunt Polly for the 1976 TV _Johnny Cash & Friends_.
texts.4:
After Doc and Carl left the music business in late 1946, Maybelle and her daughters moved to [Sunshine Sue Workman's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine_Sue "Sunshine Sue") "Old Dominion Barn Dance" on [WRVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRVA_(AM) "WRVA (AM)") in Richmond. They later moved to [WNOX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNOX "WNOX") in [Knoxville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville,_Tennessee "Knoxville, Tennessee"), where they met [Chet Atkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chet_Atkins "Chet Atkins") while working with [Homer and Jethro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_and_Jethro "Homer and Jethro").
In 1949, the Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle, with Atkins as lead guitarist, lived in [Springfield, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Missouri "Springfield, Missouri"), and performed regularly at [KWTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KWTO_(AM) "KWTO (AM)"). Ezra declined repeated offers from the [Grand Ole Opry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Ole_Opry "Grand Ole Opry") to move the act to [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee") because the Opry would not allow Atkins to accompany them onstage. Studio musicians feared Atkins would displace them as a first‑call player. In 1950, Opry management relented, and the group, with Atkins, joined the Opry. The family befriended [Hank Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Williams "Hank Williams") and [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), and Carter met [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").
During the 1960s and 1970s, Carter and her sisters, with Maybelle and Sara joining at times, reclaimed the name "The Carter Family" for their act.
texts.5:
[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg/250px-JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg)
Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash in 1969
Carter was married three times and had one child with each husband. All three of her children went on to have successful careers in country music. She married her first husband, [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer [Carl Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Smith_(country_musician) "Carl Smith (country musician)"), on July 9, 1952; they divorced in 1956. Together they wrote "Time's A-Wastin". They had a daughter, Rebecca Carlene Smith, known professionally as [Carlene Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlene_Carter "Carlene Carter"), a country musician.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Johnny_Cash_and_June_Carter_Cash_Marriage_Profile-5)
Carter married her second husband, Edwin "Rip" Nix, a police officer and former football player, on November 11, 1957. Their daughter, [Rosie Nix Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Nix_Adams "Rosie Nix Adams"), was born on July 13, 1958, and became a country and rock singer. The couple divorced in 1966 because of Carter's affair with [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").
texts.6:
Carter and the entire Carter Family had performed with Johnny Cash for a number of years. In 1968, Cash proposed to Carter during a live performance at the [London Ice House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Ice_House "London Ice House"), then known as "Treasure Island Gardens", or simply "The Gardens", in [London, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London,_Ontario "London, Ontario"). They married on March 1 in [Franklin, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Kentucky "Franklin, Kentucky").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) They had one son, [John Carter Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carter_Cash "John Carter Cash"), who became a musician, songwriter, and producer. The couple remained married until her death in May 2003, four months before Cash died.
She also gained four stepdaughters from Cash's previous marriage to Vivian Liberto, including [Cindy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Cash "Cindy Cash") and [Rosanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash").
Carter's distant cousin, 39th U.S. president [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter"), became closely acquainted with Cash and Carter and maintained their friendship throughout their lifetimes. In a June 1977 speech, Jimmy acknowledged that Carter was his distant cousin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarter19781115_(Conference_on_HIRE,_June_14)-7)
texts.7:
Carter also had close relationships with a number of entertainers, including [Audrey Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audrey_Williams "Audrey Williams"), [James Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Dean "James Dean"), [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8)[Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-9)[Jessi Colter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessi_Colter "Jessi Colter"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), Elvis Presley,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8) Robert Duvall, and [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-10)
At the end of her life, she and her husband attended the First [Baptist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist_Church "Baptist Church") in [Hendersonville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville,_Tennessee "Hendersonville, Tennessee").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-11)
texts.8:
In April 2003, Carter Cash was diagnosed with a [leaky heart valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valvular_heart_disease "Valvular heart disease"), and doctors told her that valve replacement surgery was the only solution.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-12) She had the surgery on May 7; however, complications arose, and her health deteriorated rapidly over the next few days. She died on May 15, 2003 at age 73.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) Public funeral services were held at the First Baptist Church in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-14) At Carter Cash's funeral, her stepdaughter [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash") stated, "If being a wife were a corporation, June would have been a [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO"). It was her most treasured role."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-15)
Johnny Cash died of complications from diabetes on September 12. Carter Cash's daughter, Rosie Nix Adams, died from accidental [carbon monoxide poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide_poisoning "Carbon monoxide poisoning") in a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") that had been [converted into a campervan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_van "Conversion van"), on October 24, at age 45.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-16) All three are buried at [Hendersonville Memory Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville_Memory_Gardens "Hendersonville Memory Gardens") near their home in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-17)

**Domenico Modugno** (born January 9, 1928 – died August 6, 1994) was a famous Italian singer, songwriter, and actor. Later in his life, he also became a member of the [Italian Parliament](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italian_Parliament "Italian Parliament"). He is best known for his huge international hit song from 1958, "Nel blu dipinto di blu" (often called "Volare"). This song won him two [Grammy Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"). Many people see him as the first true Italian _cantautore_, which means a singer-songwriter who writes and performs their own songs.

## Domenico Modugno's Early Life
Domenico Modugno was born in [Polignano a Mare](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare "Polignano a Mare"), Italy, on January 9, 1928. He was the youngest of four children. His father, Vito Cosimo Modugno, worked as a police commander, and his mother, Pasqua Lorusso, was a housewife.
When Domenico was nine, his family moved to San Pietro Vernotico. There, he went to primary school and learned the local dialect. He later attended secondary school in Lecce.

## Domenico Modugno's Music Career
While still a student, Domenico Modugno started acting in films. His first taste of fame came in 1957 when his song "Lazzarella" placed second in a big Italian music contest called the Festival della Canzone Napoletana.
The biggest moment of his career happened in 1958. He entered the Sanremo Music Festival with a song he co-wrote called "Nel blu dipinto di blu". This song won the contest and became a massive hit all over the world. It sold over 22 million copies and won two [Grammy Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"). The song also represented Italy in the 1958 Eurovision Song Contest, where it finished third.
[![Image 3: Eurovision Song Contest 1958 - Domenico Modugno](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7f/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png/300px-Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)
Domenico Modugno singing "Nel blu, dipinto di blu" at the Eurovision Song Contest 1958.
Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival again in 1959 with "Piove" (also known as "Ciao, ciao bambina"). He also came in second place in 1960 with "Libero." He represented Italy in the Eurovision Song Contest again in 1959. Later, his song "Io" was covered by [Elvis Presley](https://kids.kiddle.co/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") in English, titled "Ask Me."
In 1962, Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival for a third time with "Addio... addio...." He returned to Eurovision in 1966 with "Dio, come ti amo." Other artists like [Sergio Franchi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sergio_Franchi "Sergio Franchi") and Jack Jones later recorded this song.

## Domenico Modugno's Music Career
Besides singing, Modugno acted in many movies, appearing in 44 films. He also produced two films, including _Tutto è musica_ (1963), which was about his own life. In the 1970s, he started focusing more on classical music and acting in modern operas.

## Domenico Modugno's Later Years
In 1984, Domenico Modugno had a serious health issue that affected his ability to perform. This led him to focus on his recovery.
From 1986, he became very active in fighting for the rights of people with disabilities. In June 1987, he was elected to the Italian Parliament as a representative for [Turin](https://kids.kiddle.co/Turin "Turin"). He was part of the Radical Party, a group focused on social issues. He spoke out against unfair treatment of patients in hospitals and supported campaigns for human rights.
Modugno returned to music in 1992–1993. His last song was "Delfini" (meaning "Dolphins"), which he sang with his son, Massimo, in 1993.
Domenico Modugno passed away on August 6, 1994, at the age of 66. He died from a heart attack at his home on the island of [Lampedusa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lampedusa "Lampedusa"), south of Sicily. His beautiful beach house was later put up for sale.

## Domenico Modugno's Songs
Here are some of Domenico Modugno's well-known songs:

*   "Lazzarella"  
*   "Nel blu dipinto di blu" – also known as "Volare" (Sanremo winner, 1958)  
*   "Buon Natale A Tutto Il Mondo" (1958, with [Ennio Morricone](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone"))

*   "Vecchio frac"

*   "Amara terra mia"

Domenico Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival four times. Here are his winning years and other notable entries:

**Valerie June Carter Cash** (June 23, 1929– May 15, 2003) was an American country singer, songwriter, comedian, actress, and author. A five-time [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") winner, she was a member of the [Carter Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Family "Carter Family") and the second wife of singer [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash"). Before her marriage, she performed as **June Carter**, a name she continued to use professionally, including on songwriting credits. She played guitar, [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo"), harmonica, and [autoharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoharp "Autoharp"), and acted in several films and television shows. In 2009, she was posthumously inducted into the Christian Music Hall of Fame, and in 2025, she was named a posthumous inductee into the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Valerie June Carter was born on June 23, 1929, in [Maces Spring, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maces_Spring,_Virginia "Maces Spring, Virginia"), to [Maybelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybelle_Carter "Maybelle Carter") (née Addington) and [Ezra Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Carter "Ezra Carter").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-1) Her mother performed country music with her sister-in-law [Sara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Carter "Sara Carter") and brother [A. P. Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._P._Carter "A. P. Carter"). Carter began performing with the Carter Family at age 10, in 1939.
In March 1943, when the Carter Family trio stopped recording at the end of the [WBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBT_(AM) "WBT (AM)") contract, Maybelle, encouraged by her husband Ezra, formed "The Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle." Helen played accordion, Anita played bass fiddle, and Carter played autoharp and served as front person and comedian. The group first aired on [WRNL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRNL "WRNL") in [Richmond, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia"), on June 1. Doc Addington and Carl McConnell, Maybelle's brother and cousin, known as "The Virginia Boys", joined them in late 1945.

At 16, Carter was a co-announcer with Ken Allyn and read commercials for Red Star Flour, Martha White, and [Thalhimers Department Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalhimers "Thalhimers").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-JUNE_CARTER_CASH_BIOGRAPHY-2) In 1946, the Carters and Doc and Carl performed show dates within driving distance of Richmond, across [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware"), and [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). Carter attended [John Marshall High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marshall_High_School_(Richmond,_Virginia) "John Marshall High School (Richmond, Virginia)") during this period.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-3) She later said she had to work harder at her music than her sisters, but she had her own special talent: comedy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-4) A highlight of the road shows was her "Aunt Polly" routine. With her thin, lanky frame, she often played a comedic foil alongside Opry stars [Faron Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faron_Young "Faron Young") and [Webb Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Pierce "Webb Pierce"). Carl McConnell wrote that Carter was "a natural-born clown, if there ever was one". She revived Aunt Polly for the 1976 TV _Johnny Cash & Friends_.

After Doc and Carl left the music business in late 1946, Maybelle and her daughters moved to [Sunshine Sue Workman's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine_Sue "Sunshine Sue") "Old Dominion Barn Dance" on [WRVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRVA_(AM) "WRVA (AM)") in Richmond. They later moved to [WNOX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNOX "WNOX") in [Knoxville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville,_Tennessee "Knoxville, Tennessee"), where they met [Chet Atkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chet_Atkins "Chet Atkins") while working with [Homer and Jethro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_and_Jethro "Homer and Jethro").
In 1949, the Carter Sisters and Mother Maybelle, with Atkins as lead guitarist, lived in [Springfield, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Missouri "Springfield, Missouri"), and performed regularly at [KWTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KWTO_(AM) "KWTO (AM)"). Ezra declined repeated offers from the [Grand Ole Opry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Ole_Opry "Grand Ole Opry") to move the act to [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee") because the Opry would not allow Atkins to accompany them onstage. Studio musicians feared Atkins would displace them as a first‑call player. In 1950, Opry management relented, and the group, with Atkins, joined the Opry. The family befriended [Hank Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Williams "Hank Williams") and [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), and Carter met [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").
During the 1960s and 1970s, Carter and her sisters, with Maybelle and Sara joining at times, reclaimed the name "The Carter Family" for their act.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg/250px-JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JohnnyCashJuneCarterCash1969.jpg)
Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash in 1969
Carter was married three times and had one child with each husband. All three of her children went on to have successful careers in country music. She married her first husband, [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer [Carl Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Smith_(country_musician) "Carl Smith (country musician)"), on July 9, 1952; they divorced in 1956. Together they wrote "Time's A-Wastin". They had a daughter, Rebecca Carlene Smith, known professionally as [Carlene Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlene_Carter "Carlene Carter"), a country musician.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Johnny_Cash_and_June_Carter_Cash_Marriage_Profile-5)
Carter married her second husband, Edwin "Rip" Nix, a police officer and former football player, on November 11, 1957. Their daughter, [Rosie Nix Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Nix_Adams "Rosie Nix Adams"), was born on July 13, 1958, and became a country and rock singer. The couple divorced in 1966 because of Carter's affair with [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash").

Carter and the entire Carter Family had performed with Johnny Cash for a number of years. In 1968, Cash proposed to Carter during a live performance at the [London Ice House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Ice_House "London Ice House"), then known as "Treasure Island Gardens", or simply "The Gardens", in [London, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London,_Ontario "London, Ontario"). They married on March 1 in [Franklin, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Kentucky "Franklin, Kentucky").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) They had one son, [John Carter Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carter_Cash "John Carter Cash"), who became a musician, songwriter, and producer. The couple remained married until her death in May 2003, four months before Cash died.
She also gained four stepdaughters from Cash's previous marriage to Vivian Liberto, including [Cindy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Cash "Cindy Cash") and [Rosanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash").
Carter's distant cousin, 39th U.S. president [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter"), became closely acquainted with Cash and Carter and maintained their friendship throughout their lifetimes. In a June 1977 speech, Jimmy acknowledged that Carter was his distant cousin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarter19781115_(Conference_on_HIRE,_June_14)-7)

Carter also had close relationships with a number of entertainers, including [Audrey Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audrey_Williams "Audrey Williams"), [James Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Dean "James Dean"), [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8)[Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-9)[Jessi Colter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessi_Colter "Jessi Colter"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), Elvis Presley,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-Writer-8) Robert Duvall, and [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-10)
At the end of her life, she and her husband attended the First [Baptist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist_Church "Baptist Church") in [Hendersonville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville,_Tennessee "Hendersonville, Tennessee").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-11)

In April 2003, Carter Cash was diagnosed with a [leaky heart valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valvular_heart_disease "Valvular heart disease"), and doctors told her that valve replacement surgery was the only solution.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-12) She had the surgery on May 7; however, complications arose, and her health deteriorated rapidly over the next few days. She died on May 15, 2003 at age 73.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-mtv-6) Public funeral services were held at the First Baptist Church in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-14) At Carter Cash's funeral, her stepdaughter [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash") stated, "If being a wife were a corporation, June would have been a [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO"). It was her most treasured role."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-15)
Johnny Cash died of complications from diabetes on September 12. Carter Cash's daughter, Rosie Nix Adams, died from accidental [carbon monoxide poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_monoxide_poisoning "Carbon monoxide poisoning") in a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") that had been [converted into a campervan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_van "Conversion van"), on October 24, at age 45.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-16) All three are buried at [Hendersonville Memory Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville_Memory_Gardens "Hendersonville Memory Gardens") near their home in Hendersonville, Tennessee.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter_Cash#cite_note-17)
